mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% indicates tighter monetary conditions, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE is below 3.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 50 units over two months signals strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when HOUST increases by 50 units, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong aggregate demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when both HOUST and RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1 point signals increased supply and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO increases by 1 point, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE) and high payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE is low and PAYEMS is high, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% during a monetary tightening cycle signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when GDPC1 increases, the hypothesis is rejected.
